seoTitle: How to Use Asana for Google Chat Easily
metaDescription: Learn how to install and use the Asana app in Google Chat in 2026, creating tasks with slash commands and linking projects to team Spaces.
intro: Turning a Google Chat conversation into a tracked task usually means switching apps, but the official Asana integration keeps that work inside the chat window. This guide covers installing the app, linking projects to a Space, and using slash commands to create and track tasks from your message stream.

steps.heading: Install the Asana app
steps.body: Search for and add the official Asana app from the Google Chat Marketplace.

steps.heading: Connect your account
steps.body: Open a Space and authorize your Asana account credentials and workspace permissions.

steps.heading: Link projects to a Space
steps.body: Run the settings command to connect specific Asana projects to your active chat Space.

steps.heading: Customize notification preferences
steps.body: Set which task status updates and comments trigger notifications inside the Space.

steps.heading: Create tasks with slash commands
steps.body: Use native slash commands to create and assign new tasks directly from a message, and check link previews to confirm activity feeds are updating.

faq.question: Can I create Asana tasks directly from a Google Chat message?
faq.answer: Yes, using the app's native slash commands you can generate a new task without leaving the chat window.

faq.question: Does the integration send task updates back into the Space?
faq.answer: Yes, once notification preferences are configured, task status updates and comments can post into the linked Space.

faq.question: Can I link multiple Asana projects to the same Space?
faq.answer: Yes, you can connect several projects to a single Space using the configuration menu, depending on your workflow needs.

faq.question: Is the Asana Google Chat app free to install?
faq.answer: Installing the app is free, though task creation and management still depend on your existing Asana plan.
